scope: Targeted property tests verifying certificate verification authority gating (02) and observer-relative freshness SLA lag budgets (03)

properties_verified.details: All 3 canonical certificate cases from data/transport_certificates.json evaluated. Case 1 (pending outcome) correctly halts at AuthorityLaundering (NotAuthorized); Case 2 (missing verifier) routes to MissingVerifier (NotAuthorized); Case 3 (verified) routes to Accept (Authorized).

Randomized property sweep over 8 non-verified outcome types (pending, None, rejected, failed, in_progress, claimed, self_certified, unknown) verified that no unverified certificate can mint authorization. Pending triggers AuthorityLaundering; all others trigger MissingVerifier.
Verified that only an exact outcome of 'verified' can route to Accept and Authorized with certified=True and authorized=True.

All 3 canonical observer scenarios from data/observers.json evaluated. Scenario A demonstrates differential observer routing on lag=7s (dashboard AuthorizedFresh, trading_engine RefreshRequired); Scenario B handles missing lag via ConservativeInvalidate; Scenario C enforces scope authorization firewall via Refuse.
Verified functorial observer relativity: for identical packets, distinct observers evaluate independent satisfaction according to their respective declared SLA lag tolerance ceilings.
Step-function monotonicity verified across threshold sweeps: for packet lag L, an observer with tolerance T >= L is AuthorizedFresh, while T < L transitions strictly to RefreshRequired.
Fails closed on omitted or null replica lag metadata, forcing ConservativeInvalidate even when observer has an unbounded SLA tolerance budget.
Scope access firewall verified: an observer without authorized scope access is immediately Refused, strictly preceding and overriding freshness SLA checks even on 0-lag packets.
